title: Device-independent certification of tripartite quantum networks with bilocal Bell inequalities
authors: Patryk Michalski, Arturo Konderak, Remigiusz Augusiak
abstract: While quantum networks have been extensively studied as a natural extension of the standard Bell scenario with a richer correlation structure, general constructions of nonlinear Bell inequalities with self-testing properties are still largely lacking. In this work, we present a general method for constructing such inequalities in the simplest network scenario, in which two independent sources distribute bipartite quantum states to three spatially separated observers. These inequalities allow for arbitrary numbers of binary measurements and are maximally violated by maximally entangled states of the corresponding local dimensions together with sets of pairwise anticommuting Clifford observables. Importantly, their maximal quantum values can be determined analytically, which makes them particularly promising for device-independent applications. In particular, we prove that these Bell inequalities can be used to device-independently certify the underlying quantum network, including both the quantum states produced by the sources and the observables measured by all parties. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first self-testing result for quantum networks that relies solely on the maximal violation of a nonlocality witness.
summary: This paper introduces a general method to construct nonlinear Bell inequalities for tripartite quantum networks using two independent sources of entanglement. By analyzing these inequalities, the authors achieve device-independent self-testing, proving that maximal violation forces the underlying shared states and measurement observables into specific, verifiable quantum structures.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing general methods for constructing nonlinear Bell inequalities with self-testing properties specifically tailored for tripartite quantum networks.
main_result: The authors present a framework that allows device-independent certification of the entire quantum network—including both the shared states and all measured observables—by relying solely on violating a single nonlocality witness.
method: They construct nonlinear Bell inequalities using Real Row-Orthogonal and Column-Normalized (ROCN) matrices, whose maximal quantum values are analytically determined. Self-testing is established by analyzing the rank of an auxiliary matrix derived from these coefficients.
model_or_system: The model is a tripartite quantum network involving three spatially separated observers (Alice, Bob, Charlie) connected via two independent sources distributing bipartite entangled states ($ho_{AB_1}$ and $ho_{B_2C}$).
key_observables: Correlators $\langle A_x B_y C_z angle$, the nonlinear Bell inequality sum $S_h$, and the maximal quantum value $ eta_h^Q$.
important_parameters: The dimensions of measurement settings ($m$ for Alice/Charlie, $n$ for Bob) and the structure defined by the ROCN matrix $h$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on algebraic properties derived from ROCN matrices and assumes full rank conditions on auxiliary matrices to guarantee self-testing.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the bilocal network setup involving two sources ($S_1, S_2$) distributing states to Alice, Bob, and Charlie with specified measurement settings.
paper_structure: The paper develops a general framework using ROCN matrices to formulate nonlinear Bell inequalities for the tripartite setting. It then derives conditions (like full rank of matrix M) under which violating these bounds guarantees self-testing of the underlying quantum correlations and measurements.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, purely theoretical tools for verifying fundamental assumptions about quantum resources in multi-party systems without needing to trust the measurement devices themselves. This is crucial for scaling up quantum communication protocols.
